In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a theoretical framework for indoor channel modeling.
a new approach for modeling the indoor channel for geolocation systems.
the development of the unified geolocation channel model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the unified path loss model provides an approach for linking the path loss models for the three geolocation environments (macrocellular microcellular, indoor) and frequency of operation, while the unified geolocation model provides an approach that enables calculation of reflections’ gain and provides a theoretical basis for the unified geolocation channel model.

the path loss model of the indoor channel model consists of a function of the distance between the TX and RX and the frequency of the signal, and the multipath distribution model consists of a linear combination of the four distributions namely (1) Nakagami with degrees of freedom, (2) Rayleigh, (3) Rician and (4) Lognormal.
the unified geolocation indoor channel model is supported by theoretical data and it is the only channel model that is able to explain the measurement data reported in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we should design future geolocation receivers to account for the following: (1) 40-80 dB signal degradation indoors, (2) reflections with gain 1-5 dB greater than LOS gain and (3) reflections with gain greater than 5dB greater then LOS gain are extremely rare and can be ignored.
the unified geolocation channel model is a good model for the indoor channel, but it is not the best.
we need to be able to design receivers that will operate with signal to noise ratio on the order of ~10dB or higher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should never assume that we have reflections with gains greater that 5 dB greater the LOS gain.
